zip_caveats: 92831 to 92835 are Fullerton, but 92831 includes part of Placentia and the Cal State Fullerton campus area, 92833 dips into Buena Park and La Habra, and 92835 reaches toward Brea. 92834, 92836, 92837 and 92838 are PO box ZIPs. After the 2025 redraw, the official state ZIP directory lists CD-45 and CD-46 for 92831, 92832 and 92833, and CD-41 and CD-45 for 92835. CD-40 is not listed for these four ZIPs. ZIP lines are approximate; confirm your own congressional race with the registrar. For the Assembly, roughly north of Chapman and Malvern avenues is AD-59 and the south is AD-67. For the State Senate, the southern part is SD-34, which is on the ballot; the northern part is SD-37, an odd-numbered seat not up this year, so north Fullerton voters have no Senate race. Fullerton elects councilmembers by district, and only Districts 3 and 5 vote this year; the district map is at cityoffullerton.com. School district lines (Fullerton School District K-8, Fullerton Joint Union High School District, North Orange County Community College District) do not follow city lines. At the edges some addresses may fall in Placentia-Yorba Linda, Buena Park, La Habra City or Lowell Joint districts; their trustee races are not in this guide. There is no Fullerton city measure in November 2026 (the council rejected a sales tax in July) and no countywide Orange County measure; OC Measures A through O are all for other cities or school districts. Use the address lookup at ocvote.gov/vlt to see your exact ballot.

early_in_person.hours_note: Some Orange County vote centers are open Saturday, October 24 to Friday, October 30. Every center is open October 31 to November 2. Hours on those dates are 10 AM to 6 PM. On Election Day, November 3, every center is open 7 AM to 8 PM. You can use any vote center in Orange County.
early_in_person.hours_short: Orange County vote centers are open 10 AM to 6 PM every day.

request_deadline.rule: You don't need to ask for a ballot: every voter gets one in the mail. Orange County's last day to mail you a replacement was Tuesday, October 27 (7 days before Election Day). You can now get a replacement at any Orange County vote center or at the Registrar's office, 1300 S. Grand Ave., Building C, Santa Ana. You can also vote in person.

situations.short: Get a replacement at any Orange County vote center or at the Registrar's office in Santa Ana.
situations.answer: Orange County's deadline for a mailed replacement passed on October 27. You can still get a replacement ballot at any Orange County vote center or at the Registrar's office, 1300 S. Grand Ave., Building C, Santa Ana. Call (714) 567-7600 with questions.

notes: Fullerton has eight vote centers. Through Oct 30 only the Fullerton Public Library drive-thru, 353 W. Commonwealth Ave., is open; the other seven open Oct 31. Fullerton has six drop boxes. The county's map with wait times: ocvote.gov/locate.

dated.text: All eight Fullerton vote centers are open, including the Fullerton Public Library drive-thru, 353 W. Commonwealth Ave. Fullerton has six drop boxes. The county's map with wait times: ocvote.gov/locate.
